claim: SLAM/SAP signaling pathway regulates the development and function of multiple innate-like γδ T cell subsets.
source: Recently, we demonstrated that the SLAM/SAP signaling pathway regulates the development and function of multiple innate-like γδ T cell subsets.
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding by the authors in the abstract.

claim: SAP deficiency resulted in a significant loss of an immature Gzma+Blk+Etv5+Tox2+ γδT17 precursor population.
source: SAP deficiency resulted in both a significant loss of an immature Gzma+Blk+Etv5+Tox2+ γδT17 precursor population and a significant increase in Cd4+Cd8+Rorc+Ptcra+Rag1+ thymic γδ T cells.
evidence: This finding is presented in the abstract as a result of the study.

claim: SAP deficiency resulted in a significant increase in Cd4+Cd8+Rorc+Ptcra+Rag1+ thymic γδ T cells.
source: SAP deficiency resulted in both a significant loss of an immature Gzma+Blk+Etv5+Tox2+ γδT17 precursor population and a significant increase in Cd4+Cd8+Rorc+Ptcra+Rag1+ thymic γδ T cells.
evidence: This finding is presented in the abstract as a result of the study.

claim: SAP-dependent diversion of embryonic day 17 thymic γδ T cell clonotypes into the αβ T cell developmental pathway was associated with a decreased frequency of mature clonotypes in neonatal thymus.
source: SAP-dependent diversion of embryonic day 17 thymic γδ T cell clonotypes into the αβ T cell developmental pathway was associated with a decreased frequency of mature clonotypes in neonatal thymus, and an altered γδ TCR repertoire in the periphery.
evidence: This finding is presented in the abstract as a result of the study.

claim: SAP-dependent diversion of embryonic day 17 thymic γδ T cell clonotypes into the αβ T cell developmental pathway was associated with an altered γδ TCR repertoire in the periphery.
source: SAP-dependent diversion of embryonic day 17 thymic γδ T cell clonotypes into the αβ T cell developmental pathway was associated with a decreased frequency of mature clonotypes in neonatal thymus, and an altered γδ TCR repertoire in the periphery.
evidence: This finding is presented in the abstract as a result of the study.

claim: TRGV4/TRAV13-4(DV7)-expressing T cells are a novel, SAP-dependent Vγ4 γδT1 subset.
source: Finally, we identify TRGV4/TRAV13-4(DV7)-expressing T cells as a novel, SAP-dependent Vγ4 γδT1 subset.
evidence: This finding is presented in the abstract as a result of the study.

claim: SAP-dependent γδ/αβ T cell lineage commitment regulates γδ T cell developmental programming and shapes the γδ TCR repertoire.
source: Together, the data support a model in which SAP-dependent γδ/αβ T cell lineage commitment regulates γδ T cell developmental programming and shapes the γδ TCR repertoire.
evidence: This is the main conclusion presented in the abstract.

claim: γδ T cells can be broadly grouped into innate-like IFN-γ-producing γδT1, IL-4-producing γδT2, or IL-17-producing γδT17 subsets that are functionally programmed during thymic development.
source: Like αβ T cells, γδ T cells can be broadly grouped into innate-like IFN-γ-producing γδT1, IL-4-producing γδT2, or IL-17-producing γδT17 subsets that are functionally programmed during thymic development (Grigoriadou et al., 2003; Haas et al., 2012; Ribot et al., 2009; Sumaria et al., 2017), or that undergo differentiation in the periphery (Chien et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: γδ T cells can undergo differentiation in the periphery.
source: Like αβ T cells, γδ T cells can be broadly grouped into innate-like IFN-γ-producing γδT1, IL-4-producing γδT2, or IL-17-producing γδT17 subsets that are functionally programmed during thymic development (Grigoriadou et al., 2003; Haas et al., 2012; Ribot et al., 2009; Sumaria et al., 2017), or that undergo differentiation in the periphery (Chien et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Innate-like γδ T cells are highly enriched in mucosal tissues such as the skin, gut, and lung.
source: These innate-like γδ T cells are highly enriched in mucosal tissues such as the skin, gut, and lung and play critical roles in the host response to pathogens, tumor surveillance, autoimmunity, and tissue homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Innate-like γδ T cells play critical roles in the host response to pathogens, tumor surveillance, autoimmunity, and tissue homeostasis.
source: These innate-like γδ T cells are highly enriched in mucosal tissues such as the skin, gut, and lung and play critical roles in the host response to pathogens, tumor surveillance, autoimmunity, and tissue homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: IFN-γ-producing γδT1 play a critical role in tumor elimination.
source: This is perhaps best exemplified in the setting of cancer where IFN-γ-producing γδT1 have been shown to play a critical role in tumor elimination (He et al., 2010; Gao et al., 2003; Girardi et al., 2001), while γδT17 subsets promote tumor growth and metastasis (Coffelt et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2014; Rei et al., 2014; Wakita et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: γδT17 subsets promote tumor growth and metastasis.
source: This is perhaps best exemplified in the setting of cancer where IFN-γ-producing γδT1 have been shown to play a critical role in tumor elimination (He et al., 2010; Gao et al., 2003; Girardi et al., 2001), while γδT17 subsets promote tumor growth and metastasis (Coffelt et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2014; Rei et al., 2014; Wakita et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Weak TCR signal strength might contribute to the development of innate-like γδT17 subsets.
source: A significant body of data supports a model in which weak or strong TCR signal strength might contribute to the development of innate-like γδT17 (weak signal) and γδT1 (strong signal) subsets (Sumaria et al., 2017; Turchinovich and Hayday, 2011; Jensen et al., 2008; Muñoz-Ruiz et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2021), and a strong TCR signal has been suggested to be necessary for the development of the IFN-γ- and IL-4-producing γδNKT cell subset (Kreslavsky et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Strong TCR signal strength might contribute to the development of innate-like γδT1 subsets.
source: A significant body of data supports a model in which weak or strong TCR signal strength might contribute to the development of innate-like γδT17 (weak signal) and γδT1 (strong signal) subsets (Sumaria et al., 2017; Turchinovich and Hayday, 2011; Jensen et al., 2008; Muñoz-Ruiz et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2021), and a strong TCR signal has been suggested to be necessary for the development of the IFN-γ- and IL-4-producing γδNKT cell subset (Kreslavsky et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: A strong TCR signal has been suggested to be necessary for the development of the IFN-γ- and IL-4-producing γδNKT cell subset.
source: A significant body of data supports a model in which weak or strong TCR signal strength might contribute to the development of innate-like γδT17 (weak signal) and γδT1 (strong signal) subsets (Sumaria et al., 2017; Turchinovich and Hayday, 2011; Jensen et al., 2008; Muñoz-Ruiz et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2021), and a strong TCR signal has been suggested to be necessary for the development of the IFN-γ- and IL-4-producing γδNKT cell subset (Kreslavsky et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: There is evidence of a TCR-independent model in which pre-existing hard-wired transcriptional programs regulate the development of some innate-like γδT17 subsets.
source: However, there is also evidence of a TCR-independent model in which pre-existing hard-wired transcriptional programs regulate the development of some innate-like γδT17 subsets (Spidale et al., 2018), and accumulating data suggest that γδT17 programming is associated with the use of distinct signaling pathways (Laird et al., 2003; Sumaria et al., 2021; Muro et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: γδT17 programming is associated with the use of distinct signaling pathways.
source: However, there is also evidence of a TCR-independent model in which pre-existing hard-wired transcriptional programs regulate the development of some innate-like γδT17 subsets (Spidale et al., 2018), and accumulating data suggest that γδT17 programming is associated with the use of distinct signaling pathways (Laird et al., 2003; Sumaria et al., 2021; Muro et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SLAM family receptors comprise a family of nine receptors that are expressed primarily on hematopoietic cells.
source: SLAM family receptors comprise a family of nine receptors, SLAMF1 (SLAM; CD150), SLAMF2 (CD48), SLAMF3 (Ly9; CD229), SLAMF4 (2B4; CD244), SLAMF5 (CD84), SLAMF6 (Ly108; CD352), SLAMF7 (CRACC; CD319), SLAMF8 (BLAME), and SLAMF9 (SF2001; CD84H), that are expressed primarily on hematopoietic cells and which play diverse roles in immune development and function (Cannons et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Most SLAM family receptors interact in a homophilic manner.
source: Most SLAM family receptors interact in a homophilic manner, the exception to this rule being SLAMF4, which serves as the ligand for SLAMF2.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: SLAMF4 serves as the ligand for SLAMF2.
source: Most SLAM family receptors interact in a homophilic manner, the exception to this rule being SLAMF4, which serves as the ligand for SLAMF2.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: SLAM family receptor signals can be both activating or inhibitory, depending on the recruitment of cytosolic signaling adapter proteins.
source: SLAM family receptor signals can be both activating or inhibitory, depending on the recruitment of the cytosolic signaling adapter proteins SAP (encoded by Sh2d1a) and EAT-2, and inhibitory SHP-1, SHP-2, or SHIP phosphatases to immunoreceptor tyrosine switch motifs in the SLAM family receptor cytoplasmic domain (Cannons et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SLAM/SAP signaling plays a role in innate-like NKT cell development.
source: Although SLAM/SAP signaling has long been known to play a role in innate-like NKT (Nichols et al., 2005) and γδNKT (Kreslavsky et al., 2008) cell development, recent findings from multiple groups demonstrate that this pathway is also involved in the development of innate-like γδT1, γδT17 (Dienz et al., 2020) and innate-like MAIT cells (Legoux et al., 2019; Koay et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SLAM/SAP signaling plays a role in innate-like γδNKT cell development.
source: Although SLAM/SAP signaling has long been known to play a role in innate-like NKT (Nichols et al., 2005) and γδNKT (Kreslavsky et al., 2008) cell development, recent findings from multiple groups demonstrate that this pathway is also involved in the development of innate-like γδT1, γδT17 (Dienz et al., 2020) and innate-like MAIT cells (Legoux et al., 2019; Koay et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SLAM/SAP signaling is involved in the development of innate-like γδT1 and γδT17.
source: Although SLAM/SAP signaling has long been known to play a role in innate-like NKT (Nichols et al., 2005) and γδNKT (Kreslavsky et al., 2008) cell development, recent findings from multiple groups demonstrate that this pathway is also involved in the development of innate-like γδT1, γδT17 (Dienz et al., 2020) and innate-like MAIT cells (Legoux et al., 2019; Koay et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SLAM/SAP signaling is involved in the development of innate-like MAIT cells.
source: Although SLAM/SAP signaling has long been known to play a role in innate-like NKT (Nichols et al., 2005) and γδNKT (Kreslavsky et al., 2008) cell development, recent findings from multiple groups demonstrate that this pathway is also involved in the development of innate-like γδT1, γδT17 (Dienz et al., 2020) and innate-like MAIT cells (Legoux et al., 2019; Koay et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SLAM/SAP signaling plays a fundamental role in the development of a majority of the innate-like T cell lineages.
source: Together, these findings indicate that SLAM/SAP signaling plays a fundamental role in the development of a majority of the innate-like T cell lineages.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited literature.

claim: SAP-dependent innate-like T cell subsets are often characterized by highly restricted TCRs.
source: Finally, since SAP-dependent innate-like T cell subsets are often characterized by highly restricted TCRs (e.g., Vγ1+/Vδ6.3+ γδNKT; Azuara et al., 1997), we wished to identify whether specific TCR clonotypes were also associated with SAP-dependent γδT1 and γδT17 T cells.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: γδT17 developmental programming is thought to occur primarily during embryonic/neonatal thymic development.
source: γδT17 developmental programming is thought to occur primarily during embryonic/neonatal thymic development (Haas et al., 2012; Spidale et al., 2018; Havran and Allison, 1988), and is tightly linked to the expression of discrete TCR gamma and delta pairings (O'Brien and Born, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: γδT17 developmental programming is tightly linked to the expression of discrete TCR gamma and delta pairings.
source: γδT17 developmental programming is thought to occur primarily during embryonic/neonatal thymic development (Haas et al., 2012; Spidale et al., 2018; Havran and Allison, 1988), and is tightly linked to the expression of discrete TCR gamma and delta pairings (O'Brien and Born, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The resulting dataset represented a total of 5278 thymic γδ T cells from B6 (n = 2597) and B6.Sh2d1a-/- (n = 2681) γδ T cells.
source: The resulting dataset represented a total of 5278 thymic γδ T cells from B6 (n = 2597) and B6.Sh2d1a-/- (n = 2681) γδ T cells.
evidence: This is a description of the dataset generated in the study.

claim: The c8 cluster was enriched in Il17a, Il17f, Il23r, Rorc, and TRGV6/TRDV4 transcripts with limited CDR3 diversity.
source: In support of this annotation, the c8 cluster was enriched in Il17a, Il17f, Il23r, Rorc, and TRGV6/TRDV4 (IMGT nomenclature; encoding Vγ6/Vδ1) transcripts with limited CDR3 diversity, while the c0/c9 cluster was enriched in Ifng, Tbx21, Klrd1, Il2rb, Xcl1, and TRGV5/TRDV4 (encoding Vγ5/Vδ1) transcripts also with little to no diversity (Figure 1D–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 1 and 2, Havran et al., 1991; Itohara et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: The c0/c9 cluster was enriched in Ifng, Tbx21, Klrd1, Il2rb, Xcl1, and TRGV5/TRDV4 transcripts with little to no diversity.
source: In support of this annotation, the c8 cluster was enriched in Il17a, Il17f, Il23r, Rorc, and TRGV6/TRDV4 (IMGT nomenclature; encoding Vγ6/Vδ1) transcripts with limited CDR3 diversity, while the c0/c9 cluster was enriched in Ifng, Tbx21, Klrd1, Il2rb, Xcl1, and TRGV5/TRDV4 (encoding Vγ5/Vδ1) transcripts also with little to no diversity (Figure 1D–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 1 and 2, Havran et al., 1991; Itohara et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: The c0/c9 cluster was highly enriched in Cd244a (Slamf4).
source: Consistent with previous observations (Dienz et al., 2020), we noted that the c0/c9 cluster was highly enriched in Cd244a (Slamf4), and was enriched in transcripts from another SLAM family member, Slamf7 (Figure 1D, E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures and is consistent with previous observations.

claim: SLAMF7 expression was restricted to the innate-like lung CD44+CD45RB+γδT1 cell population.
source: Indeed, flow cytometric analysis revealed that SLAMF7 expression was restricted to the innate-like lung CD44+CD45RB+γδT1 cell population, and that γδT1 cells are SLAMF1-F6+F7+, while the CD44+CD45RB- γδT17 subsets are SLAMF1+F6-F7- (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The c3 cluster was enriched in Cd200, Il2rb, Nr4a1, Cd244a, Xcl1, and Tnfrsf9.
source: We identified a small CD24low/int73high44high45RBpos c3 cluster characterized by enrichment in Cd200 (whose expression is upregulated upon TCR ligation; Buus et al., 2017), Il2rb, Nr4a1, Cd244a, Xcl1, and Tnfrsf9 (encoding 4-1BB).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data and a citation.

claim: The c3 cluster represented an immature γδT1 population.
source: A high frequency of invariant TRGV5/TRDV4 clonotypes and decreased TCR clonotype diversity (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 2) suggested that c3 represented an immature γδT1 population.
evidence: This is inferred from TCR clonotype data shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: The c4 cluster represents emigrating thymic Ccr9+S1pr1+ γδ T cells.
source: The CD24low/posCD73low/pos44low/posCD45RBlow/pos c4 cluster was enriched in Ms4a4b and Ms4a6b (encoding CD20 homologues that modulate T cell activation; Xu et al., 2010; Howie et al., 2009), S1pr1, Il6ra, Cd8a, Cd8b1, and Ccr9, suggesting that the c4 cluster represents the previously described emigrating thymic Ccr9+S1pr1+ γδ T cells (Sagar et al., 2020, Figure 1C, E).
evidence: This is inferred from gene expression data and supported by citations.

claim: The c1 and c2 clusters were enriched in γδT17-associated genes such as Blk, Maf, Sox13, Ccr2, Tcf12, and Rorc.
source: The c1 and c2 clusters were enriched in γδT17-associated genes such as Blk, Maf, Sox13, Ccr2, Tcf12, and Rorc (In et al., 2017; Laird et al., 2010; Zuberbuehler et al., 2019; Narayan et al., 2012; Lu et al., 2015), as well as Sh2d1a and Ccr9 (Chen et al., 2021, Figure 1E, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data and citations.

claim: The c2 cluster was especially enriched in genes previously implicated in γδ T cell development such as Etv5, Tox, Sox4, Tcf7, Zbtb16.
source: Within these two clusters, the CD44low/posCD45RBlow c2 cluster was especially enriched in genes previously implicated in γδ T cell development such as Etv5, Tox, Sox4, Tcf7, Zbtb16 (Lu et al., 2015; Jojic et al., 2013; Malhotra et al., 2013; He et al., 2022; Fahl et al., 2021), Igfbp4, and Igf1r which were recently implicated in Th17 differentiation (DiToro et al., 2020), Tnfsf11 (RANKL) which regulates Aire+ mTEC development (Roberts et al., 2012), as well as Themis and Tox2 (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data and citations.

claim: The c2 cluster was identified as the previously described Gzma+ γδ T cell subset.
source: A high level of Gzma expression identified c2 as the previously described Gzma+ γδ T cell subset (Sagar et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data and a citation.

claim: The c2 cluster was enriched in γδT2-associated Gata3 and Il4 transcripts.
source: Interestingly, in addition to expressing γδT17-associated genes, the c2 cluster was also enriched in γδT2-associated Gata3 and Il4 transcripts (Figure 1D, E, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: The c1 cluster exhibited significantly higher levels of Il17a, Il17f, Rorc, Maf.
source: The CD44low/posCD45RBneg c1 cluster, in contrast, exhibited significantly higher levels of Il17a, Il17f, Rorc, Maf (Zuberbuehler et al., 2019), as well as Ifngr1, consistent with the c1 cluster representing immature γδT17 cells (Figure 1D–E, G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: The c1 cluster represents immature γδT17 cells.
source: The CD44low/posCD45RBneg c1 cluster, in contrast, exhibited significantly higher levels of Il17a, Il17f, Rorc, Maf (Zuberbuehler et al., 2019), as well as Ifngr1, consistent with the c1 cluster representing immature γδT17 cells (Figure 1D–E, G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: The c2 cluster was notably enriched in TRGV4-expressing cells.
source: Analysis of the c1 and c2 TCR transcripts revealed that the c2 cluster was notably enriched in TRGV4-expressing cells and that 87% of Vγ4 T cells utilized just 3 TRDV chains (50% TRDV5, 24% TRDV2-2, and 12% TRAV13-4/DV7) (Figure 1F, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by TCR transcript analysis shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: 87% of Vγ4 T cells in the c2 cluster utilized just 3 TRDV chains (50% TRDV5, 24% TRDV2-2, and 12% TRAV13-4/DV7).
source: Analysis of the c1 and c2 TCR transcripts revealed that the c2 cluster was notably enriched in TRGV4-expressing cells and that 87% of Vγ4 T cells utilized just 3 TRDV chains (50% TRDV5, 24% TRDV2-2, and 12% TRAV13-4/DV7) (Figure 1F, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by TCR transcript analysis shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: Clonotype analysis revealed a high frequency of semi-invariant TRGV4/TRDV5 and TRGV4/TRDV2-2 clonotypes previously associated with γδT17.
source: Clonotype analysis revealed a high frequency of semi-invariant TRGV4/TRDV5 and TRGV4/TRDV2-2 clonotypes previously associated with γδT17 (Wei et al., 2015; Kashani, 2015; Sim and Augustin, 1990, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by clonotype analysis and citations.

claim: The Vγ1 repertoire was dominated by TRGV1/TRDV4 clonotypes in E17 thymus.
source: Indeed, we noted that the Vγ1 repertoire, which is diverse in adult tissues, was dominated by TRGV1/TRDV4 clonotypes (35% of all TRGV1) in E17 thymus, and just two closely related semi-invariant TRGV1/TRDV4 clonotypes comprised 17.4% of all TRGV1.
evidence: This is supported by TCR repertoire analysis.

claim: Two closely related semi-invariant TRGV1/TRDV4 clonotypes comprised 17.4% of all TRGV1 in E17 thymus.
source: Indeed, we noted that the Vγ1 repertoire, which is diverse in adult tissues, was dominated by TRGV1/TRDV4 clonotypes (35% of all TRGV1) in E17 thymus, and just two closely related semi-invariant TRGV1/TRDV4 clonotypes comprised 17.4% of all TRGV1.
evidence: This is supported by TCR repertoire analysis.

claim: The location of TRGV1/TRDV4 clonotypes in the immature γδT17-related clusters suggested that they represented the dominant IL-17-producing Vγ1 clonotypes at E17.
source: The location of these clonotypes in the immature γδT17-related clusters (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) suggested that they represented the dominant IL-17-producing Vγ1 clonotypes at E17, which we verified using flow cytometry (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is inferred from clonotype location data and verified by flow cytometry.

claim: The Il4-enriched γδ T cells in cluster 2 were not immature Vγ1 γδNKT cells with canonical Vδ6.3 sequences.
source: Interestingly, while we did identify a small number of Vγ1 T cells with these canonical sequences (encoded by TRAV15-1/DV6-1 or TRAV15N-1) in our dataset, these were not present in the Il4-enriched c2 cluster.
evidence: This is based on analysis of TCR sequences in the dataset.

claim: The c5 and c7 clusters were enriched in Il2ra, Scin, Bex6, Cd5, Slamf6, Cd28, Hivep3, and cell cycle/metabolism genes.
source: The CD44posCD45RBpos c5 cluster was enriched in Il2ra, Scin, Bex6, Cd5, Slamf6, Cd28, Hivep3, and cell cycle/metabolism genes, consistent with γδ T cells that have recently developed from DN2/DN3 (Sagar et al., 2020; Scaramuzzino et al., 2022; Prinz et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data and citations.

claim: The c5 cluster is consistent with γδ T cells that have recently developed from DN2/DN3.
source: The CD44posCD45RBpos c5 cluster was enriched in Il2ra, Scin, Bex6, Cd5, Slamf6, Cd28, Hivep3, and cell cycle/metabolism genes, consistent with γδ T cells that have recently developed from DN2/DN3 (Sagar et al., 2020; Scaramuzzino et al., 2022; Prinz et al., 2006).
evidence: This is inferred from gene expression data and supported by citations.

claim: Rorc expression became apparent in the c2 cluster (Rorclow) and was significantly increased in the c1 cluster.
source: Within the c5 and c7 clusters, we noted that while there was expression of γδT17-associated genes such as Blk, Maf, Sox13, and Etv5, there was relatively little Rorc expression. Rorc expression became apparent in the c2 cluster (Rorclow) and was significantly increased in the c1 cluster (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: Flow cytometric analysis confirmed BLK and PLZF expression in CD25high E17 Vγ4 T cells, while RORγt expression was primarily observed in the CD25neg population.
source: Flow cytometric analysis confirmed BLK and PLZF expression in CD25high E17 Vγ4 T cells, while RORγt expression was primarily observed in the CD25neg population, suggesting that BLK is expressed soon after γδ T cell selection, followed by RORγt (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in figures.

claim: BLK is expressed soon after γδ T cell selection, followed by RORγt.
source: Flow cytometric analysis confirmed BLK and PLZF expression in CD25high E17 Vγ4 T cells, while RORγt expression was primarily observed in the CD25neg population, suggesting that BLK is expressed soon after γδ T cell selection, followed by RORγt (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is inferred from flow cytometry data shown in figures.

claim: These data were consistent with MAF-directed expression of Rorc.
source: These data were consistent with MAF-directed expression of Rorc (Sagar et al., 2020; Zuberbuehler et al., 2019) and suggested a c5–c7–c2–c10/c1–c8 γδT17 developmental trajectory, which was supported by trajectory inference analysis (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is inferred from the data and supported by citations and trajectory analysis.

claim: A c5–c7–c2–c10/c1–c8 γδT17 developmental trajectory was supported by trajectory inference analysis.
source: These data were consistent with MAF-directed expression of Rorc (Sagar et al., 2020; Zuberbuehler et al., 2019) and suggested a c5–c7–c2–c10/c1–c8 γδT17 developmental trajectory, which was supported by trajectory inference analysis (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by trajectory inference analysis shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The c6 population was highly enriched in Cd8a, Cd8b1, Cd4, Rag1, Rag2, Ptcra, Arpp21, and Dgkeos, consistent with cells developing along the αβ T cell lineage.
source: Finally, analysis of the CD24high73neg44neg45RBintSLAMF1posSLAMF6pos c6 population revealed that it was highly enriched in Cd8a, Cd8b1, Cd4, Rag1, Rag2, Ptcra, Arpp21, and Dgkeos, consistent with cells developing along the αβ T cell lineage (Figure 1E, G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1, Mingueneau et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data and a citation.

claim: Analysis of the Vγ1 and Vγ4 ADTs confirmed that c6 cells were not simply contaminating αβ T cells as both Vγ1- and Vγ4-expressing cells were present in the c6 cluster.
source: Analysis of the Vγ1 and Vγ4 ADTs confirmed that c6 cells were not simply contaminating αβ T cells as both Vγ1- and Vγ4-expressing cells were present in the c6 cluster (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) and analysis of the c6 TCR clonotypes revealed the presence of TRGV1, GV4, GV5, GV6, and GV7 clonotypes, none of which appeared to be specific to the c6 cluster (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by ADT and TCR clonotype analysis shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: The c6 cluster was highly enriched in Rorc, suggestive of a γδT17 phenotype, but was mostly lacking in the expression of Maf, Blk, Ccr2, and other canonical γδT17-associated transcripts.
source: Interestingly, we found that the c6 cluster was highly enriched in Rorc, suggestive of a γδT17 phenotype, but was mostly lacking in the expression of Maf, Blk, Ccr2, and other canonical γδT17-associated transcripts (Figure 1E, G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: Flow cytometric analysis of E17 TCRβnegTCRδpos γδ T cells confirmed that CD4CD8 DP γδ T cells exhibited an immature CD44lowCD25lowMAFnegBLKnegRORγtpos phenotype.
source: Indeed, flow cytometric analysis of E17 TCRβnegTCRδpos γδ T cells confirmed that CD4CD8 DP γδ T cells exhibited an immature CD44lowCD25lowMAFnegBLKnegRORγtpos phenotype (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), and that RORγt expression in the absence of BLK or MAF is a characteristic of Linneg DN thymocytes as they progress from CD44low25high DN3 to CD44low25low DN4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).

claim: SAP regulates the γδ T cell thymic developmental checkpoint at all ages.
source: Like the SAP-dependent E17 c2 and D9 c1 clusters, the adult thymus c1 and c2 clusters were enriched in γδT17-associated Blk, Etv5, Sox13, Maf, and Rorc (mostly in c2) indicating that SAP regulates this γδ T cell thymic developmental checkpoint at all ages.
evidence: This is inferred from the gene expression and cluster frequency data across different ages.

claim: There was a near complete loss of mature γδNKT cells in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult thymus.
source: Just as we observed in neonatal thymic γδ T cells, we noted a near complete loss of mature γδNKT cells (Zbtb16, Icos, and Il4-enriched γδT2 c8 cells and Tbx21, Slamf7, and Il2rb-enriched γδT1 c11 cells) as well as a decreased frequency of mature non-γδNKT γδT1 c10 cluster cells in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult thymus (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: There was a decreased frequency of mature non-γδNKT γδT1 c10 cluster cells in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult thymus.
source: Just as we observed in neonatal thymic γδ T cells, we noted a near complete loss of mature γδNKT cells (Zbtb16, Icos, and Il4-enriched γδT2 c8 cells and Tbx21, Slamf7, and Il2rb-enriched γδT1 c11 cells) as well as a decreased frequency of mature non-γδNKT γδT1 c10 cluster cells in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult thymus (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The frequency of γδ T cells with an αβ T cell-like signature in the adult thymic γδ T cell dataset was minimal.
source: Unlike the E17 and neonatal thymic datasets, however, the frequency of γδ T cells with an αβ T cell-like signature in the adult thymic γδ T cell dataset was minimal.
evidence: This is a description of the adult thymus dataset.

claim: There are multiple SAP-dependent developmental changes during neonatal and adult γδ T cell development.
source: Collectively, these data supported the presence of multiple SAP-dependent developmental changes during neonatal and adult γδ T cell development—a reduction in the CD24posCD73neg SLAMF1+SLAMF6+ cluster enriched in γδT17 development-associated transcripts, an increased frequency of immature S1pr1-enriched γδ T cells, and decreased frequencies of both γδNKT cells (γδT1 and γδT2) and non-γδNKT γδT1 cells.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings from neonatal and adult thymus data.

claim: A comparison of the frequencies of the top 100 neonate γδ TCR clonotypes between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice revealed significant changes in the overall frequency of several TRGV1 and TRGV4 clonotypes.
source: A comparison of the frequencies of the top 100 neonate γδ TCR clonotypes between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice revealed significant changes in the overall frequency of several TRGV1 and TRGV4 clonotypes (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype frequency comparison shown in Figure 5A.

claim: There was a profound loss of TRGV1 clonotypes utilizing the canonical TRAV15N-1 and TRAV15-1/TRDV6-1 γδNKT cell TCRs in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice.
source: Consistent with a SAP-dependent loss of γδNKT, we observed a profound loss of TRGV1 clonotypes utilizing the canonical TRAV15N-1 and TRAV15-1/TRDV6-1 γδNKT cell TCRs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Loss of canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes was directly tied to the significant decrease of the γδT1 c8 and γδT2 c13 clusters.
source: Loss of these clonotypes was directly tied to the significant decrease of the γδT1 c8 and γδT2 c13 clusters, in which nearly all these clonotypes resided.
evidence: This is inferred from the TCR clonotype and cluster frequency data.

claim: Within the B6 γδT2 c13 cluster the vast majority (~86%) of TCR sequences were highly restricted canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes.
source: Within the B6 γδT2 c13 cluster the vast majority (~86%) of TCR sequences were highly restricted canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes (Supplementary file 2) and nearly all of these clonotypes were also present in the γδT1 c8 cluster, consistent with the ability of γδNKT cells to produce both IFN-γ and IL-4.
evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis shown in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Nearly all canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes in the c13 cluster were also present in the γδT1 c8 cluster.
source: Within the B6 γδT2 c13 cluster the vast majority (~86%) of TCR sequences were highly restricted canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes (Supplementary file 2) and nearly all of these clonotypes were also present in the γδT1 c8 cluster, consistent with the ability of γδNKT cells to produce both IFN-γ and IL-4.
evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis shown in Supplementary file 2.

claim: The B6 γδT1 c8 cluster contained a large proportion of canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes (~46% of c8 TCRs).
source: In contrast, while the B6 γδT1 c8 cluster contained a large proportion of canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes (~46% of c8 TCRs), it also contained TCRs with a diverse pool of clonotypes that utilized TRGV1 (~70% of c8 TCRs), TRGV4, TRGV5, TRGV6, and TRGV7 that were present only in the c8 γδT1 cluster.
evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis.

claim: The B6 γδT1 c8 cluster also contained TCRs with a diverse pool of clonotypes that utilized TRGV1 (~70% of c8 TCRs), TRGV4, TRGV5, TRGV6, and TRGV7 that were present only in the c8 γδT1 cluster.
source: In contrast, while the B6 γδT1 c8 cluster contained a large proportion of canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes (~46% of c8 TCRs), it also contained TCRs with a diverse pool of clonotypes that utilized TRGV1 (~70% of c8 TCRs), TRGV4, TRGV5, TRGV6, and TRGV7 that were present only in the c8 γδT1 cluster.
evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis.

claim: In neonates, the thymic γδT1 population is a mixture of γδNKT and 'non-γδNKT' γδT1 clonotypes, and each of these clonotype pools is SAP-dependent.
source: Therefore, in neonates, the thymic γδT1 population is a mixture of γδNKT and 'non-γδNKT' γδT1 clonotypes, and each of these clonotype pools is SAP-dependent.
evidence: This is inferred from the TCR sequence analysis.

claim: A closer examination of the neonatal thymic TRGV4 clonotypes revealed a significant decrease in the frequencies of γδT17-associated clonotypes with a germline-encoded TRDV5.
source: Interestingly, a closer examination of the neonatal thymic TRGV4 clonotypes revealed a significant decrease in the frequencies of γδT17-associated clonotypes with a germline-encoded TRDV5 (Kashani, 2015; Figure 5B), some of which were identical to those that were redistributed to the αβ T cell-like c6 cluster in E17 γδ T cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype analysis shown in Figure 5B and a citation.

claim: When TRGV4/TRDV5 clonotypes were mapped to their D9 clusters, there was a significant decrease in the frequency of TRGV4/TRDV5 clonotypes in the mature γδT17 c6 cluster.
source: When these clonotypes were mapped to their D9 clusters, we noted a significant decrease in the frequency of TRGV4/TRDV5 clonotypes in the mature γδT17 c6 cluster (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype mapping shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The immature E17 γδ TCR clonotypes that were redirected to the αβ T cell pathway in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice were underrepresented among the mature B6.Sh2d1a-/- neonatal γδ T cells.
source: Taken together, these data indicated that the immature E17 γδ TCR clonotypes that were redirected to the αβ T cell pathway in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice were underrepresented among the mature B6.Sh2d1a-/- neonatal γδ T cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the TCR clonotype data across E17 and D9 timepoints.

claim: SAP-deficiency results in a significant impairment in γδ T cell function in the periphery.
source: We previously demonstrated that SAP-deficiency results in a significant impairment in γδ T cell function in the periphery (Dienz et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding by the authors.

claim: γδ T cell IL-17 production is impaired in the lungs of young B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice, but this had largely corrected itself as the mouse reached maturity.
source: Specifically, we observed that γδ T cell IL-17 production is impaired in the lungs of young mice, but that this had largely corrected itself as the mouse reached maturity.
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding by the authors.

claim: Both Vγ1 and Vγ4 IFN-γ production were significantly impaired in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult lung and spleen.
source: In contrast, we observed that both Vγ1 and Vγ4 IFN-γ production were significantly impaired in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult lung and spleen.
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding by the authors.

claim: The initial annotation of the B6 lung γδ T cell transcriptome revealed the presence of 11 clusters.
source: Our initial annotation of the B6 lung γδ T cell transcriptome revealed the presence of 11 clusters of the lung γδ T cells that we annotated based on cluster-specific gene expression and TRGV and TRDV usage (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a description of the lung γδ T cell dataset.

claim: Based on their expression of signature cytokines and transcription factors, 2 γδT17 clusters (c1 and c4), 4 γδT1 clusters (c2, c3, c7, and c9), 1 γδTNKT-like cluster (c10), and a Cd24-enriched cluster (c5) were identified.
source: Based on their expression of signature cytokines and transcription factors, we identified 2 γδT17 clusters (c1 and c4), 4 γδT1 clusters (c2, c3, c7, and c9), 1 γδTNKT-like cluster (c10) with very few cells, as well as a Cd24-enriched cluster (c5) (Figure 6B, C, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: The c1 and c4 γδT17 clusters were enriched in Slamf1.
source: Consistent with previous observations, we noted that the c1 and c4 γδT17 clusters were enriched in Slamf1 and that the c2/c3/c7/c9 γδT1 clusters were enriched in Slamf7 and Slamf6 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The c2/c3/c7/c9 γδT1 clusters were enriched in Slamf7 and Slamf6.
source: Consistent with previous observations, we noted that the c1 and c4 γδT17 clusters were enriched in Slamf1 and that the c2/c3/c7/c9 γδT1 clusters were enriched in Slamf7 and Slamf6 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Flow cytometric analysis revealed that SLAMF7 expression was restricted to the innate-like lung CD44+CD45RB+γδT1 cell population.
source: Indeed, flow cytometric analysis revealed that SLAMF7 expression was restricted to the innate-like lung CD44+CD45RB+γδT1 cell population, and that γδT1 cells are SLAMF1-F6+F7+, while the CD44+CD45RB- γδT17 subsets are SLAMF1+F6-F7- (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: γδT1 cells are SLAMF1-F6+F7+, while the CD44+CD45RB- γδT17 subsets are SLAMF1+F6-F7-.
source: Indeed, flow cytometric analysis revealed that SLAMF7 expression was restricted to the innate-like lung CD44+CD45RB+γδT1 cell population, and that γδT1 cells are SLAMF1-F6+F7+, while the CD44+CD45RB- γδT17 subsets are SLAMF1+F6-F7- (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The c1 cluster corresponded to Vγ4 γδT17 (primarily TRGV4/TRDV5 and TRGV4/TRDV2-2).
source: Further annotation using V(D)J profiling revealed that the c1 cluster corresponded to Vγ4 γδT17 (primarily TRGV4/TRDV5 and TRGV4/TRDV2-2) while the c4 cluster corresponded to lung Vγ6 (TRGV6/TRDV4) (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by V(D)J profiling shown in Figure 6E and Supplementary file 6.

claim: The c4 cluster corresponded to lung Vγ6 (TRGV6/TRDV4).
source: Further annotation using V(D)J profiling revealed that the c1 cluster corresponded to Vγ4 γδT17 (primarily TRGV4/TRDV5 and TRGV4/TRDV2-2) while the c4 cluster corresponded to lung Vγ6 (TRGV6/TRDV4) (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by V(D)J profiling shown in Figure 6E and Supplementary file 6.

claim: The c10 cluster was enriched in Zbtb16, Il4, and Icos.
source: The c10 cluster was enriched in Zbtb16, Il4, and Icos (Figure 6B, C) as well as TRGV1/TRAV15N-1 and TRGV1/TRDV6 sequences (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6) consistent with γδNKT cells.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figures 6B and 6C.

claim: The c10 cluster was consistent with γδNKT cells.
source: The c10 cluster was enriched in Zbtb16, Il4, and Icos (Figure 6B, C) as well as TRGV1/TRAV15N-1 and TRGV1/TRDV6 sequences (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6) consistent with γδNKT cells.
evidence: This is inferred from gene expression and TCR sequence data.

claim: The TRAV15N-1 and TRDV6 sequences in the c10 cluster were, for the most part, non-canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes.
source: We did note, however, that the TRAV15N-1 and TRDV6 sequences in the c10 cluster were, for the most part, non-canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes, suggesting a degree of flexibility in the TRAV15N-1 and TRDV6 CDR3 sequences that can be utilized by γδNKT cells.
evidence: This is based on analysis of TCR sequences in the c10 cluster.

claim: Vγ4 γδT1 cells exhibited a striking preference in the usage of TRAV13-4(DV7).
source: Interestingly, while the γδT1 c2/c3/c7/c9 clusters contained primarily Vγ1 and Vγ4 T cells as expected, we noted that Vγ4 γδT1 cells exhibited a striking preference in the usage of TRAV13-4(DV7), and that TRGV4/TRDV7 pairings accounted for 80% of all Vγ4 clonotypes in the γδT1 clusters (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis shown in Figure 6E and Supplementary file 6.

claim: TRGV4/TRDV7 pairings accounted for 80% of all Vγ4 clonotypes in the γδT1 clusters.
source: Interestingly, while the γδT1 c2/c3/c7/c9 clusters contained primarily Vγ1 and Vγ4 T cells as expected, we noted that Vγ4 γδT1 cells exhibited a striking preference in the usage of TRAV13-4(DV7), and that TRGV4/TRDV7 pairings accounted for 80% of all Vγ4 clonotypes in the γδT1 clusters (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis shown in Figure 6E and Supplementary file 6.

claim: Analysis of the γδT1 TRAV13-4/DV7 CDR3 sequences revealed a high level of diversity that showed no evidence of clonal expansions.
source: Analysis of the γδT1 TRAV13-4/DV7 CDR3 sequences revealed a high level of diversity that showed no evidence of clonal expansions (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by CDR3 sequence analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Vγ1 γδT1 cells exhibited a more mild pairing preference where 44% of the γδT1 clonotypes utilized TRAV15N-1, TRAV15-1/DV6-1, or TRAV15D-2/DV6D-2 and 13% utilized TRAV13-4/DV7.
source: Vγ1 γδT1 cells, in contrast, exhibited a more mild pairing preference where 44% of the γδT1 clonotypes utilized TRAV15N-1, TRAV15-1/DV6-1, or TRAV15D-2/DV6D-2 and 13% utilized TRAV13-4/DV7 (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype analysis shown in Supplementary file 6.

claim: These data formed a comprehensive map of B6 lung γδ T cell transcriptomes and revealed that lung innate-like γδT1, like γδT17 and γδNKT, are all characterized by preferential TCR γ- and δ-chain pairings.
source: Together these data formed a comprehensive map of B6 lung γδ T cell transcriptomes and revealed that lung innate-like γδT1, like γδT17 and γδNKT, are all characterized by preferential TCR γ- and δ-chain pairings.
evidence: This is a summary of the lung γδ T cell data.

claim: Vγ4 γδT1 exhibited a distinct preference for the utilization of TRAV13-4(DV7) chains with diverse CDR3.
source: This was especially notable for Vγ4 and our data suggested that Vγ4 γδT1 exhibited a distinct preference for the utilization of TRAV13-4(DV7) chains with diverse CDR3.
evidence: This is a summary of the Vγ4 γδT1 TCR data.

claim: Lung γδ T cell IFN-γ production is deficient in Sh2d1a-deficient mice.
source: Consistent with our previous observation that lung γδ T cell IFN-γ production is deficient in Sh2d1a-deficient mice (Dienz et al., 2020), we observed a decrease in the frequency of the γδT1 c2, c3, and c7 clusters (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding by the authors and is consistent with the current data.

claim: There was a decrease in the frequency of the γδT1 c2, c3, and c7 clusters in B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
source: Consistent with our previous observation that lung γδ T cell IFN-γ production is deficient in Sh2d1a-deficient mice (Dienz et al., 2020), we observed a decrease in the frequency of the γδT1 c2, c3, and c7 clusters (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 7B.

claim: There was a striking decrease in the frequency of TRGV4/TRDV7-expressing cells in the lungs of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice.
source: Moreover, we observed a striking decrease in the frequency of TRGV4/TRDV7-expressing cells in the lungs of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7C, D, Supplementary file 6), and we noted that we found no evidence of a compensatory increase in the frequency of other TRDV-expressing lung Vγ4 γδT1 cells in the B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
evidence: This is supported by TCR expression analysis shown in Figures 7C and 7D and Supplementary file 6.

claim: There was no evidence of a compensatory increase in the frequency of other TRDV-expressing lung Vγ4 γδT1 cells in the B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
source: Moreover, we observed a striking decrease in the frequency of TRGV4/TRDV7-expressing cells in the lungs of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7C, D, Supplementary file 6), and we noted that we found no evidence of a compensatory increase in the frequency of other TRDV-expressing lung Vγ4 γδT1 cells in the B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the TCR expression analysis.

claim: The SAP-dependent decrease in TRAV13-4/TRDV7 was independently confirmed in both lung and spleen using qPCR.
source: We independently confirmed this SAP-dependent decrease in TRAV13-4/TRDV7 in both lung and spleen using qPCR (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and we demonstrated a significant decrease in the number of CD44+SLAMF7+ Vγ4 T cells in both the lungs and spleen of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was a significant decrease in the number of CD44+SLAMF7+ Vγ4 T cells in both the lungs and spleen of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice.
source: We independently confirmed this SAP-dependent decrease in TRAV13-4/TRDV7 in both lung and spleen using qPCR (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and we demonstrated a significant decrease in the number of CD44+SLAMF7+ Vγ4 T cells in both the lungs and spleen of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The decreased lung γδT1 did not appear to be due to an SAP-dependent decrease in homeostatic proliferation, nor to increased apoptosis.
source: The decreased lung γδT1 did not appear to be due to an SAP-dependent decrease in homeostatic proliferation, nor to increased apoptosis, since we observed no significant change in lung γδ T cell BrdU incorporation or Annexin V staining in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation and Annexin V staining data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was a loss of the c10 γδT2 cluster in B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
source: In addition to the decrease in lung γδT1, we also noted a loss of the c10 γδT2 cluster consistent with the enrichment in SAP-dependent γδNKT TCRs in this cluster, and we observed an increased frequency of the Vγ4 γδT17 c1 cluster (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 7B.

claim: There was an increased frequency of the Vγ4 γδT17 c1 cluster in B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
source: In addition to the decrease in lung γδT1, we also noted a loss of the c10 γδT2 cluster consistent with the enrichment in SAP-dependent γδNKT TCRs in this cluster, and we observed an increased frequency of the Vγ4 γδT17 c1 cluster (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 7B.

claim: A comparison of the lung Vγ4 c1 γδT17 CDR3 sequences between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice revealed significant alterations in the γδT17 c1 cluster TCR repertoire.
source: Indeed, a comparison of the lung Vγ4 c1 γδT17 CDR3 sequences between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice revealed significant alterations in the γδT17 c1 cluster TCR repertoire.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from CDR3 sequence comparison.

claim: There was a decreased frequency of TRGV4 chains that exhibited a germline-encoded CDR3γ (CSYGYSS) in B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung Vγ4 c1 γδT17.
source: Specifically, we noted a decreased frequency of TRGV4 chains that exhibited a germline-encoded CDR3γ (CSYGYSS) and an increased frequency of TRGV4 chains with a CDR3γ exhibiting evidence of N/P additions (CSYG(X)YSS).
evidence: This is supported by CDR3 sequence analysis.

claim: There was an increased frequency of TRGV4 chains with a CDR3γ exhibiting evidence of N/P additions (CSYG(X)YSS) in B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung Vγ4 c1 γδT17.
source: Specifically, we noted a decreased frequency of TRGV4 chains that exhibited a germline-encoded CDR3γ (CSYGYSS) and an increased frequency of TRGV4 chains with a CDR3γ exhibiting evidence of N/P additions (CSYG(X)YSS).
evidence: This is supported by CDR3 sequence analysis.

claim: These changes were associated with a significant shift in the usage of TRDV2-2 CDR3δ sequence usage.
source: These changes were associated with a significant shift in the usage of TRDV2-2 CDR3δ sequence usage (Figure 7F) and an altered c1 TCR clonotype frequency in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is supported by CDR3 sequence analysis shown in Figure 7F.

claim: There was an altered c1 TCR clonotype frequency in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice.
source: These changes were associated with a significant shift in the usage of TRDV2-2 CDR3δ sequence usage (Figure 7F) and an altered c1 TCR clonotype frequency in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype frequency analysis shown in Figure 7G.

claim: Vγ4 γδT1 preferentially utilize the TRAV13-4(DV7) chain in the lung.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that Vγ4 γδT1 preferentially utilize the TRAV13-4(DV7) chain in the lung and that the SAP-dependent decrease in peripheral γδ T cell IFN-γ production is not due to dysregulated cytokine production, but rather due to a specific loss of innate-like γδT1 subsets.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lung γδ T cell data.

claim: The SAP-dependent decrease in peripheral γδ T cell IFN-γ production is not due to dysregulated cytokine production, but rather due to a specific loss of innate-like γδT1 subsets.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that Vγ4 γδT1 preferentially utilize the TRAV13-4(DV7) chain in the lung and that the SAP-dependent decrease in peripheral γδ T cell IFN-γ production is not due to dysregulated cytokine production, but rather due to a specific loss of innate-like γδT1 subsets.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lung γδ T cell data.

claim: The adult lung γδT17 TCR repertoire is altered in SAP-deficient mice.
source: This finding, together with our finding that the adult lung γδT17 TCR repertoire is altered in SAP-deficient mice, suggests that SLAM/SAP signaling plays a role in shaping the γδ TCR repertoire.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lung γδT17 TCR repertoire data.

claim: SLAM/SAP signaling plays a role in shaping the γδ TCR repertoire.
source: This finding, together with our finding that the adult lung γδT17 TCR repertoire is altered in SAP-deficient mice, suggests that SLAM/SAP signaling plays a role in shaping the γδ TCR repertoire.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TCR repertoire data.

claim: SAP plays a critical role in the development of IFN-γ and IL-4-producing γδNKT cells.
source: Within the γδ T cell lineage, SAP plays a critical role in the development of IFN-γ and IL-4-producing γδNKT cells (Azuara et al., 1997), as well as in γδT1 and γδT17 (Dienz et al., 2020), but exactly when during γδ T cell development SAP functions, and how it exerts these effects is unknown.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SAP plays a critical role in the development of γδT1 and γδT17.
source: Within the γδ T cell lineage, SAP plays a critical role in the development of IFN-γ and IL-4-producing γδNKT cells (Azuara et al., 1997), as well as in γδT1 and γδT17 (Dienz et al., 2020), but exactly when during γδ T cell development SAP functions, and how it exerts these effects is unknown.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SAP mediates its effects on immature, uncommitted thymic γδ T cells.
source: Here, we provide evidence that SAP mediates its effects on immature, uncommitted thymic γδ T cells and that it works to simultaneously promote progression through the γδT17 developmental pathway while inhibiting the diversion of γδ T cells into the αβ T cell pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: SAP works to simultaneously promote progression through the γδT17 developmental pathway while inhibiting the diversion of γδ T cells into the αβ T cell pathway.
source: Here, we provide evidence that SAP mediates its effects on immature, uncommitted thymic γδ T cells and that it works to simultaneously promote progression through the γδT17 developmental pathway while inhibiting the diversion of γδ T cells into the αβ T cell pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: The redirection of γδ T cell clonotypes into the αβ T cell pathway at E17 is associated with a decreased frequency of these mature clonotypes in neonatal thymus.
source: The redirection of γδ T cell clonotypes into the αβ T cell pathway at E17 is associated with a decreased frequency of these mature clonotypes in neonatal thymus, and an altered γδT17 TCR repertoire in the periphery.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TCR clonotype data across E17 and D9 timepoints.

claim: The redirection of γδ T cell clonotypes into the αβ T cell pathway at E17 is associated with an altered γδT17 TCR repertoire in the periphery.
source: The redirection of γδ T cell clonotypes into the αβ T cell pathway at E17 is associated with a decreased frequency of these mature clonotypes in neonatal thymus, and an altered γδT17 TCR repertoire in the periphery.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TCR clonotype data.

claim: Vγ4/Vδ7 T cells are a novel, SAP-dependent IFN-γ-producing Vγ4 γδT1 subset.
source: Finally, we identify Vγ4/Vδ7 T cells as a novel, SAP-dependent IFN-γ-producing Vγ4 γδT1 subset.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lung γδ T cell data.

claim: SAP regulates the balance of innate-like γδT1/γδT2/γδT17 subsets during thymic development and in the periphery.
source: Altogether, these findings suggest that SAP regulates the balance of innate-like γδT1/γδT2/γδT17 subsets during thymic development and in the periphery.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.
